verdict.root_cause: At 20:55:21 cartservice logged an orderly hosting-lifetime shutdown and then emitted nothing for the remaining five minutes of the window [tr_aef3c0d8efc6]; one second later the change log records an image-reference update on cartservice to `...v1.2.1-cartservice-hotfix.2` by platform-automation [tr_43e2b50377c9]. The replacement never resumed serving: cart logs stay silent while every one of 10 sampled failing checkout traces terminates with the error flag on the leaf CartService/GetCart span, with near-zero self time in checkoutservice's own spans [tr_35955453bf63], and checkoutservice logs show orders entering PlaceOrder from ~20:56:49 onward without the payment/email/message-write completion lines that accompanied earlier successful orders [tr_161a559ef3a0]. checkoutservice itself has no changes in the window [tr_d6b858e8bc87], no error-severity logs [tr_161a559ef3a0], and no service-wide error step-up at onset [tr_e19a0159dcc4] — it is the caller reporting a dead dependency. The failing artifact is the cartservice hotfix image that took the place of a healthy process and did not come back up; checkout and frontend errors follow mechanically from GetCart being unavailable.
verdict.reasoning: Three independent signals converge on the same second. The change log puts an image swap on cartservice at 20:55:22 [tr_43e2b50377c9]; cartservice's own logs show a clean SIGTERM-style shutdown at 20:55:21 followed by five minutes of total silence, with normal traffic served right up to 20:55:17 and no exception or stack trace beforehand [tr_aef3c0d8efc6] — i.e. the process was stopped for the rollout, not killed by an in-process fault. What distinguishes this from a routine rolling update is that nothing came back: no startup banner, no further cart operation traces. The failure mode seen from above matches exactly — all 10 failing traces share one shape and die at the CartService/GetCart leaf, with checkoutservice spans carrying near-zero self time, so checkout is not the author of the error, it is propagating one [tr_35955453bf63]. checkoutservice log lines corroborate: order entry continues but the downstream completion sequence stops after ~20:56:49 [tr_161a559ef3a0]. Ownership is settled negatively too: checkoutservice has zero recorded changes in a 24-hour window [tr_d6b858e8bc87] and its aggregate error ratio actually fell relative to baseline with only a late brief spike [tr_e19a0159dcc4], so nothing about checkoutservice explains the onset. The two configuration hypotheses on cartservice that could have produced a bad_config verdict are excluded by their own revert records: REDIS_ADDR was reverted ~2.2h before onset and the traffic-shaping container removed ~2.5h before onset [tr_43e2b50377c9]. Fast failures of 1.5-4.5ms at the deepest error span rule out a latency/timeout mechanism [tr_35955453bf63]. That leaves the running artifact itself as the wrong thing: the fix is to revert the image reference to the pre-hotfix tag, which the automation's own history shows it has done three times before [tr_43e2b50377c9].
open_questions: No container or pod state was ever queried — we infer the new cartservice image failed to start from log silence alone. Whether it is crash-looping, stuck pulling the image, failing a readiness probe, or was simply never scheduled is unestablished, and each implies a slightly different fix.

cartservice emits no calls_total series under that service_name label in either window [tr_d7bc36981895], so there is no server-side confirmation of cart errors at all; the entire cart-side failure picture rests on log absence plus client-side trace spans.

The pre-existing nonzero checkoutservice error ratio in the baseline window [tr_e19a0159dcc4] is unexplained and may indicate a second, unrelated degradation predating 20:55 — the earlier revert cycles of this same hotfix may be its source.
The change record shows the prior image value as null rather than a concrete previous tag [tr_43e2b50377c9], so the exact artifact to roll back to is not named in the evidence.

Only checkoutservice and cartservice were investigated. Of 12 services in the blast radius with 4 unmeasured edges crossed, no evidence rules out a concurrent independent failure elsewhere that the cart outage is masking.
Whether cartservice recovered after 21:00:36 is outside every queried window; if the automation loop reverted the hotfix as it has previously, the incident may have self-resolved.

alternatives.root_cause: The new cartservice container starts but is killed for exceeding a memory or CPU limit, so cart is repeatedly down rather than statically broken.
alternatives.why_not: No memory, CPU or restart-count metric was ever collected for cartservice [tr_d7bc36981895], so this is unfalsified rather than supported. It also predicts intermittent recovery windows with fresh startup logs between kills, and the logs show flat, unbroken silence after a single clean shutdown [tr_aef3c0d8efc6]. Note the remediation is the same either way, which lowers the operational cost of this ambiguity.

alternatives.root_cause: cartservice's Redis/cache backend became unavailable at ~20:55, and the cart process exited or failed to re-establish its connection on restart.
alternatives.why_not: cartservice logged no cache endpoint, connection failure or timeout text in the 20:54:51-20:55:21 lines immediately preceding shutdown [tr_aef3c0d8efc6], and both REDIS_ADDR edits were reverted hours before onset [tr_43e2b50377c9]. The coincidence of shutdown with the image update to within one second is a far tighter explanation than an unlogged backend failure. Redis was never directly queried, however, so this is not fully closed.

proposal.expected_effect: Redeploying cartservice at its pre-20:55:22 image should restore a serving cart process: cart-service logs in Loki resume routine GetCartAsync/AddItemAsync lines, ending the silence since 20:55:21; sampled checkout traces stop terminating on an error-flagged leaf CartService/GetCart span; checkoutservice logs resume the payment/email/message-write completion lines after each PlaceOrder entry. No cart-side error-ratio metric exists (cartservice emits no calls_total series), so confirmation must come from cart logs plus client-side traces.
proposal.if_wrong: Falsified if cart logs are still silent 5 minutes after the recreate (failure is image-pull, scheduling, or readiness rather than the artifact), or if cart logs resume but checkout traces still error at the GetCart leaf (fault is on the cart-to-Redis path), or if failing traces had already stopped before the action landed (the automation loop self-reverted).
proposal.risk: The prior image is recorded as null, so the rollback may resolve to no valid tag and leave cartservice down longer. A concurrent platform-automation apply/revert cycle on the same hotfix could flap the container. If the real defect is process/environment state rather than the image, this restart-equivalent may mask it briefly and it will recur. The unexplained pre-existing checkoutservice error ratio would remain untouched.
proposal.blast_radius: cartservice only during the recreate; its inbound callers frontend and checkoutservice see connection resets for the recreate duration, and loadgenerator-driven checkout requests in flight will fail.

triage_judgement.reasoning: Critical alerts on checkout and frontend plus the load generator, all simultaneous, describe user-facing order-path failure that cannot be dismissed. No open incidents to attribute it to, and the alert pattern alone does not distinguish a bad deploy from a failing downstream dependency.
